title: Limits of Holdout Model Selection for Adversarial Instrumental-Variable Regression under Misspecification
banked_reason: Sound negative result for a note-defined common-audit TRAE hybrid, but below the field novelty floor because no published TRAE or DeepIV workflow uses the exact refuted architecture.
gap_reasons: negative-target-missing: The negative theorem refutes a note-defined common-audit blind-training path but names no published paper, estimator, or workflow that uses that path; the cited TRAE and RDIV results are only positive comparison classes, so the required negative-result positioning and the field novelty floor are not established.
The published workflows differ materially from the proved hybrid architecture; repairing the field-tier negative target would require a materially new theorem, not a faithful source/prose correction.
proof_attempt_summary: The run first attempted a misspecified adaptive TRAE oracle inequality inspired by Regularized DeepIV, but an independent validity gate refuted candidate-specific validation because weaker critic classes mechanically receive smaller adversarial scores. A root-changing common-audit construction then yielded a sound negative theorem: an exact failure frontier (0, B^2] with attained endpoint B^2, exhaustive path-selector and signed-affine aggregation failure, and a supremum-sharp 4B^2 clipping constant. The result was downgraded because this architecture is a note-defined hybrid rather than a workflow used by either cited paper; obtaining field-tier positioning requires a materially new theorem tied faithfully to a published estimator.
tldr: For the note-defined hybrid that combines candidate-specific adversarial training with a shared absolute-convex holdout audit, the paper proves the computable training-coverage distance identity, an exact nonzero collapsed-path failure frontier \((0,B^2]\) with attained endpoint \(B^2\), and failure of every signed or affine combination of an entirely collapsed trained path. Separately, it proves the deterministic envelope \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2\) with supremum-sharp coefficient \(4\). These are architecture-level diagnostics for the note-defined hybrid. Tan--Syrgkanis discrepancy-selected TRAE and Li--Lan--Syrgkanis--Wang--Uehara Regularized DeepIV are positive neighboring comparators, not workflows refuted by the theorem.
gap: Tan and Syrgkanis prove positive discrepancy-selected TRAE rates under the assumptions of their Proposition 3.12, including critic-closeness or witness-coverage structure. Li, Lan, Syrgkanis, Wang, and Uehara use a different positive workflow in Section 8 and Algorithm 2: held-out Best-ERM or Convex-ERM compares candidates through a shared explicit learned-operator loss. Neither result studies the note-defined hybrid in which each candidate is trained against its own adversarial critic body and a common absolute-convex audit later selects only among the already-trained path. The paper therefore does not claim that either published workflow fails.
fill: The mathematical contribution is the training-coverage distance identity; a genuine two-atom exact-image witness with zero target, audit, and image defects; the exact attainable collapsed-path error frontier \((0,B^2]\); exhaustive failure of all random, data-dependent, or oracle-dependent signed and affine combinations of that collapsed path; and, independently, the supremum-sharp deterministic clipping constant \(4B^2\). The result diagnoses the note-defined hybrid only. A negative theorem about an accurately named published workflow would require a materially different construction and proof.
